sources.years: Verified working paths: budget2019-20 … budget2025-26 at /budget{YYYY-YY}/doc/eb/sbe{19..22}.pdf (all 200); budget2011-2012 … budget2018-2019 at /budget{YYYY-YYYY}/ub{YY-YY}/eb/sbe{N}.pdf (200; demand numbering differs — in 2011-12 the MoD demands were Nos. 20–27: MoD, Defence Pensions, Army, Navy, Air Force, Ordnance Factories, R&D, Capital Outlay). sources.notes: Nothing in Demands 19–22 is state- or city-resolved: a scan of the four 2025-26 demands for state/city names found only 'Jammu' (in 'Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry', Demand 19). keyFacts: BE 2025-26 (net): Demand 20 Defence Services Revenue ₹3,11,732.30 cr; Demand 21 Capital Outlay ₹1,80,000.00 cr; Demand 22 Defence Pensions ₹1,60,795.00 cr (gross ₹1,68,795 cr less ₹8,000 cr deposit-account recovery); Demand 19 MoD Civil ₹28,682.97 cr — https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/eb/sbe20.pdf, sbe21.pdf, sbe22.pdf, sbe19.pdf
Actual 2023-24: Revenue ₹2,90,442.92 cr, Capital ₹1,54,256.28 cr, Pensions ₹1,42,092.99 cr, MoD Civil ₹22,712.09 cr — same four PDFs (Actuals column)

Pay & Allowances, BE 2025-26 (Demand 20): Army ₹1,13,756.24 cr, Air Force ₹21,017.03 cr, Navy ≈₹9.8k cr (RE 2024-25 ₹9,835.52 cr; BE column truncated in extraction — re-read), Army civilians ₹8,039.74 cr — https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/eb/sbe20.pdf

Agnipath cost sits inside Demand 20 as a separate head per service: Army 1.12 'Agnipath Scheme' Actual 2023-24 ₹2,542.32 cr → BE 2024-25 ₹5,207.28 cr → RE 2024-25 ₹6,274.66 cr; Navy 2.08 ₹258.17 → ₹352.00 → ₹579.42 → BE 2025-26 ₹772.29 cr; Air Force 3.06 ₹281.91 → ₹420.00 → ₹618.00 → BE 2025-26 ₹853.00 cr — https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/eb/sbe20.pdf

Capital by service is published only as Actuals: 2023-24 Army ₹28,594.42 cr, Navy ₹50,762.62 cr, Air Force ₹60,708.41 cr (of ₹1,54,256.28 cr total); BE/RE capital is a single undivided figure (₹1,72,000 cr BE 2024-25, ₹1,59,500 cr RE 2024-25, ₹1,80,000 cr BE 2025-26) — https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/eb/sbe21.pdf
Pensions by service, BE 2025-26 gross: Army ₹1,41,751.00 cr, Air Force ₹17,553.50 cr, Navy ₹9,463.80 cr — https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/eb/sbe22.pdf

Standing Committee on Defence, 18th LS 1st Report (Dec 2024): total Defence Budget incl. MoD (Civil) and Pensions ₹6,21,940.85 cr for 2024-25 = 12.90% of total Central Government Expenditure and 1.91% of GDP — https://sansad.in/getFile/lsscommittee/Defence/18_Defence_1.pdf?source=loksabhadocs

PRS 2025-26: total defence allocation Rs 6,81,210 crore, 13% of central government expenditure (17% in 2014-15); defence grew 9% a year vs 10% for total central expenditure, 2013-14 to 2025-26 — https://prsindia.org/budgets/parliament/demand-for-grants-2025-26-analysis-defence
SIPRI India military expenditure, current US$ m: 2000 14,288; 2010 46,090; 2020 72,815; 2024 85,597; 2025 92,057 — https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/SIPRI-Milex-data-1949-2025_v1.2.xlsx
World Bank/SIPRI India military expenditure % of GDP: 2000 2.95; 2009 3.13 (peak); 2020 2.80; 2024 2.27 — https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/IND/indicator/MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS?format=json&per_page=100

Demand numbering changed: in Budget 2011-12 MoD held Demands 20–27 (MoD; Defence Pensions; Army; Navy; Air Force; Ordnance Factories; R&D; Capital Outlay), from 2018-19 onward Demands 19–22 (MoD Civil; Defence Services Revenue; Capital Outlay; Defence Pensions) — https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2011-2012/ub2011-12/eb/sbe22.pdf vs https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2018-2019/ub2018-19/eb/sbe20.pdf

No state or city resolution exists in Demands 19–22: the only geographic token in the four 2025-26 PDFs is 'Jammu' in 'Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry' (Demand 19, BE 2025-26 ₹2,074.03 cr) — https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/eb/sbe19.pdf
probes.recommendation: Build the union-defence series directly from indiabudget.gov.in: one documented table per year FY2009-10 (actuals) to FY2025-26 (BE) with columns revenue / capital / pensions / MoD-civil, service-wise pay & allowances and Agnipath heads from Demand 20, service-wise pensions from Demand 22, and service-wise capital from the Actuals column of Demand 21 only (flag BE/RE capital as unsplit). Use two URL patterns (/budget{Y}/doc/eb/sbe{19-22}.pdf for 2019-20+, /budget{YYYY-YYYY}/ub{YY-YY}/eb/sbe{N}.pdf for 2011-12 to 2018-19) and read the demand name from the PDF header because numbering shifted in the 2010s. Fill FY2000–FY2009 totals from SIPRI's local-currency financial-year sheet (reported tier, different definition — show both denominators) and % GDP from the World Bank mirror of SIPRI, never mixing the two in one line. Use Standing Committee on Defence PDFs via sansad.in/getFile (iterate 16–18 Lok Sabha) for projection-vs-allocation tables, committee commentary and CAG paragraphs, and PRS (CC BY 4.0) for narrative cross-checks only. Record CAG, MoD/DESW, Open Budgets India, loksabhadocs and Wayback as voids with the dates probed and re-test them from another network before publishing any figure that depends on them. State on the page, in plain words, that the Union defence budget is not resolved below the all-India level — the footprint-by-state story must come from other families (cantonments, DPSU/ordnance locations, Coast Guard and BRO units, procurement winners), not from these demands.

CAPF total (CRPF, NSG, BSF, ITBP, CISF, AR, SSB, accounting) Actual 2024-25 ₹1,04,824.10 cr → BE 2026-27 ₹1,16,789.30 cr; CRPF BE 2026-27 ₹38,517.93 cr, BSF ₹29,567.64 cr, CISF ₹16,828.85 cr, ITBP ₹11,324.08 cr, SSB actual 2024-25 ₹9,593.88 cr, Assam Rifles BE 2026-27 ₹8,796.68 cr, NSG ₹1,422.47 cr — https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe51.pdf
Intelligence Bureau Actual 2024-25 ₹4,013.19 cr → BE 2026-27 ₹6,782.43 cr, of which capital jumps to ₹2,549.54 cr (from ₹257.01 cr RE 2025-26) — https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe51.pdf

Delhi Police BE 2026-27 ₹12,503.65 cr (plus ₹342.50 cr police-infrastructure capital); J&K Police BE 2026-27 ₹9,925.50 cr; SPG actual 2024-25 ₹532.22 cr; NATGRID actual 2024-25 ₹248.42 cr — https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe51.pdf

Enforcement Directorate (Demand 35, Dept of Revenue) actual 2024-25 ₹516.09 cr, BE 2025-26 ₹550.75 cr, RE 2025-26 ₹606.50 cr — https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe35.pdf

probes.recommendation: Build the union-home series straight from indiabudget.gov.in SBE PDFs: they are text-extractable, licence-free official records (tier documented), 200 on predictable per-year paths back to FY2000-01, and each file carries Actual/BE/RE so a 27-year CAPF-by-force, IB, Delhi Police, MPF, SRE-LWE, Nirbhaya series can be assembled with ~27 small downloads per demand — but write a per-year demand-number map first (Police was Demand 47 in 2000-01, 51 in 2026-27) by reading page-1 titles, and record that NIA, NCB, BPR&D, NCRB sit unbroken inside 'Central Police Organisations' and that R&AW is not disclosed anywhere (publish that absence, do not estimate). Take ED from Demand 35 and CBI from Demand 74 the same way. Use PRS DFG analyses (CC-BY 4.0, 2017-18 to 2026-27) only as the reported-tier cross-check and as the index of vacancy/strength footnotes, and the MHA Annual Reports (2005-06 to 2024-25, reachable today despite the FCRA-sweep void — update DATA_SOURCES.md) for sanctioned strength, state-wise MPF/SRE releases and procurement narrative. For Parliament, drive the undocumented but working sansad.in LS question JSON API (paginate per session, filter ministry client-side; answer PDFs are the primary record) and the elibrary.sansad.in DSpace API for Standing Committee on Home Affairs reports; the sansad.in committee pages and RS APIs are a shell/504 today. Declare BPR&D, CBI/DoPT, CAG, NIA/NCB, BSF/ITBP/SSB/AR portals and Open Budgets India as voids with the routes above, and keep state-police strength (BPR&D DoPO) as the family's largest open gap pending a data.gov.in API key or browser-grade fetch.

probes.recommendation: Build the procurement-industry domain on three documented spines that are reachable today: (1) PIB MoD releases fetched with curl (not WebFetch, which gets 403) — DAC AoN releases give date, service, items and aggregate ₹ crore only; contract-signing releases give vendor, ₹ crore, buyer and date and are the one official place private groups (L&T, BEML, Bharat Forge, TASL, etc.) are named per contract; enumerate PRIDs via WebSearch site:pib.gov.in and the ministry POST on allRel.aspx; (2) the MoD Annual Report PDFs on ddpmod.gov.in (text layer, 11.5 MB) for the production-by-ownership-class, exports, licence-count, offset and corridor series 2018-19 to 2024-25; (3) indiabudget.gov.in Demands 20/21/22 (plus pensions) for the budget series. Shareholding and order-book data for the eight DPSUs and the listed privates come from screener.in pages (reported tier) linked onward to the filing PDFs, since NSE and the BSE API are void. SIPRI is reported-tier (TIV, not rupees) — use for supplier-share trend only and read the register in the app, not the fact sheet, for per-deal rows. Treat defproc.gov.in and GeM as voids (CAPTCHA / 000) and slice MoD, CAPF and police buyers from the CPPP mirror already in research/raw/cppp via the Phase H2 security.py. The named-licensee question has no portal answer: route it through Lok Sabha written-answer annexures on sansad.in (PDF) mirrored by PIB, and through each company's annual report; record 'licence holder' edges only when such a document names the company. Do not state per-item AoN costs, France/Israel supplier percentages, or any vendor for an AoN — none of those are in the primary texts read.

probes.recommendation: Build the pay-and-pensions series from indiabudget.gov.in as the spine: one PDF per demand per year (Defence Services Revenue, Capital, Defence Pensions) from FY2000-01 (budget_archive) to FY2026-27 (live), mapping demand numbers per year from each file's first page (they shift: Pensions = 21 in 2019-20→2021-22, 22 from 2022-23; per-service demands 20–26 before 2016-17; the 2016-17→2018-19 directories need the budget20YY-20YY/budget.asp index, not yet probed). Tier these documented; derive pay-to-capital and pension-share yourself and cross-check against PRS (CC BY 4.0), which should be cited as reported only where it adds committee observations the sandbox cannot reach (eparlib, loksabhadocs, rajyasabha all blocked). For the 7th CPC use the DoE PDF at the exact 'cenetral-pay_document' path; pull Level 3 → Level 17/18 cells and the four MSP rates. For Agnipath and OROP use PIB via curl (WebFetch is 403'd by PIB): the Agniveer pay table and the ₹8,450 cr/yr OROP revision are primary; the Agnipath pension-saving estimate exists only in press (The Wire/ORF/ThePrint) and must be ingested as reported with the military's later disowning as the contra. For CAPF workload use the MHA-hosted PQ PDFs (RS 1036/2024 gives five-year VR, resignation and suicide tables); for CAPF salary share open MHA DDG Vol II (Demand 50 Police) — Vol I is Demand 49 and its CRPF lines are not the force budget. State police: BPR&D DoPO is the structural void — substitute IJR 2025/2022 (CC BY 4.0, cites DoPO tables) for per-capita and per-personnel spend, and PRS State of State Finances for committed-expenditure shares, because rbidocs.rbi.org.in (all RBI data files) is blocked. Among the five target states only UP's police demand PDF opened (Grant 026, URL pattern confirmed); Maharashtra's GR portal is reachable for pay-matrix GRs but no GR was opened; KA/TN/WB finance and police hosts are all 000 — record them as voids, use PRS state pages (no police line for MH/UP) and the wbxpress ROPA mirror as reported, and never publish exam-prep-site pay figures. Before downgrading any void, run the source-retrieval skill (archive.org for bprd.nic.in DoPO PDFs and desw.gov.in OROP tables).

gaps.prompt: Repository /home/user/india-corporate-intelligence. You are a reconnaissance agent for the force-finance page, family `state-allied-bodies`: the state-funded bodies that carry force or its support and sit outside the Police major head — Home Guards and Civil Defence, fire and emergency services, prisons, forensic science laboratories, the state police housing corporations and the state police welfare funds. critic.cityResolution: From what the probes actually opened, the money India spends on force resolves at three distinct levels and the page should say so in these words. At Union level, every rupee is resolvable to the line item: the four Ministry of Defence demands (revenue, capital, pensions, MoD Civil) and the MHA Police demand are text-extractable PDFs on indiabudget.gov.in with Actual/BE/RE columns back to FY2000-01 (defence to FY2009-10 actuals via 2011-12 files), giving force-by-force CAPF, Intelligence Bureau, Delhi Police, J&K Police, SPG, NATGRID, ED (Demand 35), CBI (Demand 74) and Nirbhaya transfers (Demand 101) — but these documents carry no geography at all (the only place-name in the defence demands is 'Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry'), NIA, NCB, BPR&D and NCRB are unbroken inside 'Central Police Organisations', and R&AW is not disclosed anywhere. At state level, total police revenue expenditure per state per year is resolvable from RBI State Finances Appendix II (HTML tables; four states per page; 2023-24 accounts to 2025-26 BE in the current edition, earlier editions not yet probed) and the all-states police total from Appendix Table 5 (₹1,87,826.7 cr in 2023-24 accounts), cross-checked against PRS state budget analyses (reported tier; eight large states read live, 2016-17 onward); police strength, vacancies and spend-per-officer by state are NOT yet resolvable at documented tier because BPR&D is void and only secondary re-tabulations (IJR, dataful, PRS footnotes) were reached; prisons, fire, Home Guards and forensic budgets by state were not probed. At city level, exactly one city is resolved: Delhi, whose police is a Union line (Delhi Police actual 2024-25 ₹12,133.16 cr, BE 2026-27 ₹12,503.65 cr, plus the Delhi Police infrastructure capital line) — and even there only the police, not GNCTD-funded prisons, fire or Home Guards. Every other city's police money sits inside its state's Police head and is not separable from the published state document; Mumbai's RTI and tender pages and the state GePNIC portals were reached but yielded no commissionerate budget. What CAN give a city a rupee figure and a vendor name is procurement (Safe City/CCTV awards, commissionerate tenders, Delhi Police Housing Corporation awards on CPPP) and footprint (cantonments, DPSU plants, CAPF and command headquarters), none of which has yet been read beyond a landing page; until it is, the page prints 'inside the state's police head' for every city except Delhi rather than a number.
critic.summary: Completeness review of the force-finance reconnaissance. Only three of the seven probe families reached this critic in full (union-defence, union-home, and state-city-police up to its data.gov.in entry); the task text was truncated there, so the four remaining families were not assessed and this is stated as a limit. The three visible families are strong on the Union demands (indiabudget.gov.in PDFs, predictable paths, licence-free, documented tier with reason) and on RBI State Finances for state police totals, and honest about the big voids (BPR&D, CAG, MoD/DESW, Open Budgets India, GeM, Wayback). Six gaps are returned as probe prompts: (1) state-funded allied bodies — Home Guards, Civil Defence, fire, prisons, forensics, police housing corporations, welfare funds; (2) Union-to-state police transfers (MPF, SRE, SIS, CAPF deployment recoveries, Finance Commission) and the police-per-lakh denominators; (3) Union Territories, the J&K/Ladakh 2019 break and Delhi's GNCTD-funded prisons/fire/Home Guards; (4) Coast Guard, BRO, Defence Estates, cantonments and defence land disputes as the only geography of the defence rupee; (5) Agniveer intake and services' sanctioned-vs-held strength plus arms-export figures and the licensed-producer denominator; (6) Nirbhaya Safe City CCTV vendors and commissionerate-level procurement as the only genuinely city-resolved money. Fourteen weak-evidence items are listed, the most consequential being: the RBI Appendix II figures whose state ordering is unconfirmed, the internally inconsistent Demand 50 reading (Cabinet Secretariat ₹69.52 vs ₹72.35 cr; total smaller than its NSCS component), the CGA/PIB/DoE/force-portal entries that are landing-page 200s with wish-list fields and unreasoned 'documented' tiers, the IJR and NCRB field lists that were not read from the fetched pages, the Lok Sabha annexure example that is about Agniveer reservation rather than police strength, and the MHA AR modernisation table whose context the probe itself left unconfirmed. The city/state/Union resolution paragraph is written for the spec to quote: Union lines are fully resolvable but carry no geography; state police totals are resolvable (RBI, PRS) but strength and allied bodies are not yet documented-tier; Delhi Police is the only city budget, and city resolution elsewhere can come only from procurement and footprint records that have not yet been read past their landing pages.

fills.recommendation: Build the transfers series from three documented primaries that are reachable today and reconcile them against each other: (1) MHA Annual Report annexures (2024-25 Annexures IV, XVIII, XIX, XX; earlier years from the same index) for SRE-NE and MPF/ASUMP releases by state and year — budget an OCR step because the annexure pages are scanned images; (2) the MHA Par2017 mirror of Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha answers (deterministic path par<YYYY>-pdfs/<LS|RS><DDMMYYYY>/<qno>.pdf) — LS UQ 494 (2018-19 to 2023-24) and LS UQ 4862 (2020-21 to 2024-25) already give allocation, release and utilisation-certificate columns per state with a clean text layer, so prefer them as the machine-readable spine and use the AR annexures as the cross-check; (3) Demand 51 and Statement 22 of the Expenditure Budget for the Union-level totals and recoveries. Record LWE-SRE, J&K-SRE and CAPF deployment-charge recoveries as 'aggregate only' until a state-wise parliamentary answer is opened, and keep the per-battalion rate figures at reported tier with the news source named, since the 2019 MHA policy letter was not found. For denominators, divide by the RGI/NCP 2011-36 projections (NHM mirror, documented) for the 1 January year of each strength table, say so in the caption, and take state police strength from PRS Tables 15/22 and the IJR raw workbook at reported tier until BPR&D DoPO is fetched from outside the sandbox — the exact DoPO 2023 and 2024 file names are now known, so a single manual download would lift the whole per-lakh and per-100-sq-km series to documented. Re-run the sansad API crawl with 5-15 s back-off and per-page persistence to recover the lsapps annex URLs; do not rely on its server-side filters, which are ignored. Note that this year's indiabudget.gov.in /doc/eb/ is the 2026-27 budget and year-stamped paths 404, so pin the budget year in every citation.

keyFacts: Demand numbers shifted three times: 2019-20 (Police 48, A&N 49, Chandigarh 50, DNH 51, Daman & Diu 52, Lakshadweep 53, Delhi 54, Puducherry 55) → 2020-21 (DNH&DD merged at 51, Ladakh new at 52, Transfers to J&K new at 55, Puducherry 56) → 2021-22 (+2: Police 50, J&K 57, Puducherry 58) → 2022-23 onward stable (Police 51, A&N 52, Chandigarh 53, DNH&DD 54, Ladakh 55, Lakshadweep 56, Delhi 57, J&K 58, Puducherry 59). https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/budget2020-21/doc/eb/sbe55.pdf

J&K Police first appears in the Union Police demand at BE 2024-25 (9,789.42 cr; prior columns '...'), not 2020-21; series: RE 2024-25 8,665.94, Actual 2024-25 8,553.38, BE 2025-26 9,325.73, RE 2025-26 9,097.44, BE 2026-27 9,925.50 cr. https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe51.pdf

Transfers to J&K (Demand 58) BE series 2020-21 → 2026-27: 30,757.00; 30,757.00; 35,581.44; 35,581.44; 42,277.74; 41,000.07; 43,290.29 cr; Actual 2024-25 46,000.06. Nearly all is 'Central Assistance to UTs… to meet its resource gap'. https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe58.pdf

The J&K UT budget for 2020-21 to 2024-25 was passed by Parliament through J&K Appropriation Bills (2023-24 outlay 1,18,500 cr per News on AIR; 2020-21 1,01,428 cr per press) — these documents are not under indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/; from 2025-26 the J&K Assembly passes it (PRS: expenditure 1,06,641 cr). https://prsindia.org/budgets/states/jammu-and-kashmir-budget-analysis-2025-26

Ladakh Police is funded inside Demand 55 (Ladakh), not Demand 51: Demand 51 has zero Ladakh mentions; Demand 55 names only 'Police and Fire Control' capital 13.65 / 11.15 / 11.33 / 8.51 cr. https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe55.pdf

The five UT demands carry no separate police, jails, fire or Home Guards establishment row — only one small capital scheme each (A&N 'Police and Fire Control' 26.71 BE 26-27; Chandigarh 'Police Housing' 76.05; DNH&DD 'Police Welfare Schemes' 22.16; Lakshadweep 'Police' 6.74). https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe52.pdf

Delhi: Delhi Police is item 5 of the Union Police demand (Actual 2021-22 11,131.48 cr in the 2023-24 document); Transfers to Delhi (Demand 57) is only 1,348.01 cr BE 2026-27 with no force line; PRS states 'police is with the Centre' and the GNCTD budget analysis carries no police/prisons/fire row. https://prsindia.org/budgets/states/delhi-budget-analysis-2026-27

GNCTD-funded force lines surfaced only in press: 674 cr for firefighting infrastructure (Delhi budget 2026-27, Deccan Herald) and 10 cr Tihar relocation survey (2025-26, The Print); Home Guards and Prosecution figures not found. https://www.deccanherald.com/india/delhi/watch-cm-rekha-gupta-presents-delhi-govts-rs-103700-crore-budget-for-2026-27-3942506

Pre-2019 J&K state: Home department 5,954 cr of 80,313 cr total expenditure in BE 2018-19 incl. 100 cr capital Modernisation of Police Force (PRS; source documents at jakfinance.nic.in unreachable, 502). https://prsindia.org/budgets/states/jammu-and-kashmir-budget-analysis-2018-19

Puducherry: own legislature budget 2025-26 of 13,600 cr with central assistance 3,432.18 cr (News on AIR), matching Union Demand 59 BE 2025-26 3,432.20; Demand 59 BE 2026-27 3,517.88. finance.py.gov.in has an expired certificate. https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/eb/sbe59.pdf

PRS DFG Home Affairs 2025-26: UT grants 67,238 cr, J&K + Ladakh = 68% of UT grants, and the grants 'do not include police expenditure for Delhi and J&K police'. https://prsindia.org/budgets/parliament/demand-for-grants-2025-26-analysis-home-affairs

fills.recommendation: Ingest the Union Expenditure Budget demands as the documented spine for this family: for each year 2019-20 → 2026-27 pull the UT demands by the per-year demand-number map above (not by a fixed number) and record (i) each UT's grand total and 'Other Establishment' as the force-inclusive ceiling, (ii) the one named police/fire capital scheme per UT, (iii) Transfers to Delhi / J&K / Puducherry totals, and (iv) Demand 51 item 6 'Jammu & Kashmir Police' from BE 2024-25 onward and item 5 'Delhi Police' for all years. State plainly, with these records as source: Delhi Police and (from 2024-25) J&K Police are Union-funded under Demand 51; Ladakh Police sits inside Demand 55; Delhi's prisons, fire and Home Guards and Puducherry's police are funded by the UT legislatures' own budgets, which the Union carries only as block transfers (Demands 57 and 59). Correct the union-home probe's expectation: J&K Police enters the Union demand in 2024-25, and from 2020-21 to 2023-24 it lived in the Parliament-passed UT budget that is not on indiabudget.gov.in. Treat the UT-level police/jails/fire split, the GNCTD Home Department lines, the Puducherry Police demand and the pre-2019 J&K Home demand as declared voids with press/PRS as reported-tier placeholders, and schedule a retry of rbidocs (Appendix II parts 3 and 8), saiindia.gov.in UT accounts and finance.py.gov.in from outside the sandbox, since those three would move the voids to documented.

keyFacts: MHA approved ₹3,080.16 crore for Safe City projects in 8 cities (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai), funded from the Nirbhaya Fund and the MHA budget — MHA Annual Report 2024-25 para 14.12, printed p. 296 — https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/AREnglish_24032026.pdf

₹1,577.76 crore had been released by MHA as Central assistance for Safe City in the 8 cities as of FY 2024-25 (Women Safety Division box, printed p. 288) — https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/AREnglish_24032026.pdf

Original approved cost was ₹2,919.55 crore (Feb 2019), Centre:State 60:40 except Delhi fully Central-funded; funds released to five projects at that date — https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1562727

City-wise releases 2018-19 / 2019-20 / 2020-21 (₹ crore): Mumbai 87.47/56.17/Nil; Kolkata 47.57/8.00/Nil; Chennai 169.37/71.41/Nil; Hyderabad 83.14/39.94/Nil; Ahmedabad 51.55/42.87/37.64; Lucknow 62.89/Nil/26.54; Delhi 64.67/268.60/Nil; Bengaluru 167.26/Nil/Nil (RS reply 24 Mar 2021) — https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1707345

Lucknow Safe City sanctioned at ₹194.44 crore (1 Nov 2018), to be implemented by Uttar Pradesh Police with municipal and transport bodies — https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/pressreleasesafecityprojectinLucknow_01112018.pdf

Bengaluru Safe City SI: Honeywell Automation India Ltd, order dated 28 Sep 2021, ₹496.57 crore incl. taxes (2-yr CAPEX + 5-yr OPEX), >7,000 cameras at >3,000 locations plus ICCC — Reg.30 filing — https://www.honeywell.com/content/dam/honeywellbt/en/documents/downloads/india-hail/announcements/disclosure-under-regulation-30-october-20-2021-honeywell-wins-bengaluru-safe-city-project.pdf

Delhi Police's public e-tender API (POST /Public_VIew/Public_Tender) returns 100 rows of which exactly one is a genuine notice (catering at PS Parliament Street, issued 2026-05-04); the award/status endpoint returns 3,546 rows, none with a real contractor or value — https://tender.delhipolice.gov.in/Public_VIew/Public_Tender

Mumbai Police's Tender page lists 122 NIT PDFs (ids 532–659, Nov 2025–Sep 2026), all from the Addl. CP (Motor Transport): tyres, batteries, clutch repairs, boat equipment — no CCTV or Safe City notice — https://mumbaipolice.gov.in/Tender

Delhi Police Housing Corporation Ltd has 27 live works NITs on CPPP (e.g. 04/DPHCL/ENGG/NIT/2026-27, women-hostel quarters at Civil Lines, published 02-Oct-2026); AOC listing is CAPTCHA-gated so 0 award rows resolved live — https://etenders.gov.in/eprocure/app?page=FrontEndTendersByOrganisation&service=page

Kolkata Police has 21 live NITs on wbtenders (WBKP/CP/NIT-216…222, Sept 2026, all small works), Greater Chennai Police 1 (BDDS equipment, 2026_POLIS_706840_1) on tntenders, DGP Mumbai 1 and MSPHWC 3 on mahatenders — none Safe City-related — https://wbtenders.gov.in/nicgep/app?page=FrontEndTendersByOrganisation&service=page

CCTNS: approved outlay ₹2,000 crore (2009), ₹1,550 crore released by Apr 2018, Bihar and Rajasthan then unable to onboard a System Integrator — https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCTNS_Briefportal24042018.pdf

C-DAC Chennai is the designated CCTNS System Integrator for Goa, Lakshadweep and Mizoram (incl. O&M and ICJS 2.0 integration); AR 2024-25 names C-DAC Pune for CCTNS 2.0 — https://www.cdac.in/index.aspx?id=service_details&serviceId=CCTNS
